It reproduces with zero variance across 6 independent reset-reconfigure-run cycles and 96 total AHB-bank observations (0 of 96 exceptions), with FCB_STAT 0x000f0002 confirmed every cycle (the fabric did configure each time) and a DEVICE_ID sanity read of 0x40200001 confirmed every cycle (the DAP/AHB read path itself is sane -- it returns a different, correct value at a different address, so it is not simply stuck or globally broken). It does NOT by itself resolve T22's open question of where the fault sits (a toolchain/bitgen-encoding bug that would also reproduce on L48, versus something L64-package- or silicon-specific) -- T22 already showed every desk-computable layer of this exact bitstream (cycle-sim, routed-JSON pip-tree reconstruction against mcu_hrdata_lanes.csv, bitgen's cross-net mux-ownership check) independently agrees the intended encoding is 0x4147414d, and nothing new was added at that layer this session. method: one continuous OpenOCD session (single process, no re-attach between cycles) running 6 full reset-bracketed cycles. Each cycle: reset halt, then load_image the fabric bin at 0x20002000, load_image the firmware bin at 0x20000000, set pc/sp, resume, sleep 500ms, halt, mdw the firmware's 8-word mailbox at 0x20001000 (FCB_STAT, BANK+0x0, BANK+0x4, BANK+0x40, post-write-readback of BANK+0x0, a stability flag versus the hardcoded 0x4147414d expectation, a completion sentinel, one unused word), mdw the known-good DEVICE_ID address 0x03000100 once as a read-path sanity check, then 12 further direct mdw reads of AHB 0x60000000 with no reconfigure in between (in-config read-time check). After all 6 cycles: a plain reset (flash-boot) plus shutdown. Zero flash writes at any point in this trial (including the board-identification dump above, which is read-only)

bit_level_analysis: 0x4147414d XOR 0x795fe3dd = 0x3818a290: 10 of 32 bits differ (popcount(a)=12, popcount(b)=22), not a single stuck lane. This rules out the single-bad-codeword failure shape seen in the unrelated qualification/counter2_carry_seam_routed.json rebaseline (one bad BBMUXE_PAIR[43] codeword produced exactly one never-varying bit, cnt[1]). Getting an identical wrong 10-bit pattern on two independent physical dice from a conduction-blind, congestion-blind, purely combinational constant fan-out is very hard to explain as an analog/silicon-margin effect (it would require the same roughly one-third of 32 wide-fanout lanes to fail in the identical direction on two separate chips); a deterministic bitgen/selector-encoding defect that reproduces identically on any unit built from this exact bitstream is far more consistent with the evidence.
routing_evidence: Parsed AG32-Docs/tools/l64_bringup_20260818/constant_slave_routed.json PACKER_GND_NET / PACKER_VCC_NET ROUTING pip-trees (the same artifact T22 used for its independent routed-JSON reconstruction). This design fan-out uses X14Y11_RMUX03 -> X13Y11_BBMUXE09 and X14Y11_RMUX03 -> X13Y11_BBMUXE05 directly at the MCU-edge boundary funnel, plus seven distinct BBMUXW00-BBMUXW06 entrances. RMUX03 is one of exactly the two feeder codewords AGaMEMnon commit 48cda69 (Fix two transposed boundary-mux codewords, 2026-08-14) found wrong in the hand-typed bbmuxe_fanin.csv dict, with an identical failure signature described in that commit message (a structurally valid but wrong selector, 0 unmapped reported, only silicon disagrees, one lane that never varies). Both commits are confirmed ancestors of the fc6919c2 build (git merge-base --is-ancestor 48cda69 7247e134 and 183e9b6 7247e134 both true), so their fixes/changes ARE included in the build under test -- meaning either the 48cda69 fix is incomplete (a further wrong codeword in the same table not caught by the two-entry dict-vs-harvest diff), or 183e9b6 new BBMUXW admission logic independently introduces a different wrong-selector class for some of the 10 wrong bits, or both interact.
